$comment: Core declarations. Read at boot; the binaries are NOT. Each entry is metadata the
Rust registry stores as a CoreDescriptor so the UI can decide which core a game
needs without loading anything.
`kind` decides how a fetched module is instantiated:
libretro    - a real core built by scripts/build-core.sh. The JS runtime
instantiates it as its own wasm module (see core-runtime.js) and
hands Rust a handle.
placeholder - bytes go to Rust, which substitutes its diagnostic pattern core.
Geometry and timing below are the real values for the system, so
the pacer and renderer are already configured correctly.
`systems` is many-to-many with cores: mGBA and Gambatte both declare `gb`, and
Genesis Plus GX declares `genesis` and `sms`. `priority` breaks the tie — higher
wins, and the losers become the alternatives the UI offers on a ROM card. The
convention here is 100 for a real core and 10 for a placeholder, so a diagnostic
stand-in can never become the default for a system a real core already covers.
Ties are broken by core id, so ordering never reshuffles between loads.
The values here are a hint for the loading UI. Once content is loaded, whatever the
core reports through retro_get_system_av_info supersedes them.
`targetFps` values are true hardware refresh rates, not rounded to 60. A core
running at 60.0988 against a 60.000 Hz display is why the frame pacer exists.

cores.name: FCEUmm
cores.notes: Built from libretro/libretro-fceumm against wasi-libc. Real emulation.

cores.name: mGBA
cores.notes: Built from libretro/mgba via CMake + wasi-sdk. Real emulation; also runs GB/GBC, which is why Gambatte is declared alongside it as an alternative.

cores.name: Genesis Plus GX
cores.notes: Built from libretro/Genesis-Plus-GX against wasi-libc, with wasm setjmp/longjmp for the Musashi 68000 address-error traps. Real emulation of Mega Drive, Master System, Game Gear and SG-1000; it picks which from the content extension, so the launch path must pass a filename. Base geometry here is the Mega Drive's; Master System content reports 256x192 once loaded.

cores.name: SMS Plus GX
cores.notes: The Master System specialist, declared as the alternative to Genesis Plus GX. Still a placeholder, which makes it the useful case to test with: launching the built-in Master System cart on it produces the diagnostic pattern instead of the cart's magenta playfield, so the pixels prove which core the override actually selected.

cores.name: Gambatte
cores.notes: Declared to exercise the subcore path: gb and gbc resolve to mGBA by default and to this entry when the user picks it. Still a placeholder, so choosing it runs the diagnostic pattern core — which is exactly what makes the switch visible.

cores.name: Snes9x
cores.notes: Built from libretro/snes9x — the first C++ core, compiled with clang++ against wasi-sdk's libc++ and linked by the C++ driver. Real emulation. The max geometry is the core's own: 1024x478 covers hi-res and interlaced modes, so the video staging buffer is sized for them once rather than being resized mid-session.

cores.$comment: Phase 2 only. Declared so the library can show them; the UI refuses to launch them in the browser because they need JIT.
